findings.location: amendment.json item A3; HOST_INTERFACE_SPEC.md (effective) 5.3 SERVER row (OBSERVER and BROKER inherit it)
findings.finding: In answer to R1-4, A3 now says 'seccomp can check only the open flags, so the role's SELinux domain limits what it reads to selinuxfs status and policy, cgroup and /proc files and its own code'. As a statement about the SELinux domain, that is narrower than both the reviewed SELinux matrix and W01's own rows. In architecture/selinux-matrix-v2/matrix.json (v4), planeon_server_t also reads planeon_server_cred_t (its credential, which the sealed-credential path needs), planeon_run_t, the observer and broker socket files, planeon_bpf_pin_t and planeon_seal_t. planeon_observer_t reads planeon_observer_cred_t, which the OBSERVER row also states ('read-only to policy credential'). The broker opens the worker executable for W5. SERVER's CPython base has an unconditional read-only openat for its runtime. A W04 test or a W03 policy author taking the row literally would forbid reads the matrix grants and the rows require.
findings.requiredChange: Scope the sentence to what seccomp cannot do, for example: 'seccomp checks only the open flags; which files the role may read (for these inspection reads: selinuxfs status and policy, cgroup and /proc files, its own code) is decided by its SELinux domain (matrix v4 READ grants)'. Do not present that list as the domain's complete read set.

findings.location: amendment.json item A2; HOST_INTERFACE_SPEC.md 5.3 WORKER row, SELinux column
findings.finding: A2 says the worker has 'no execute_no_trans on any type and no transition out of the domain (SELinux matrix v4 A24-A32, A37, A60.18)'. The first half holds: A60.18 is the worker's per-source execute_no_trans closure over every type, declared or not, and A37 covers the entrypoint, interpreter and container types. The cited assertions do not establish the second half. A24-A31 constrain transitions only into the planeon domains (contain, maint, the daemon roles, worker, writer), and A32 covers only dyntransition. No assertion covers a worker transition into the qualk8s_* domains. The matrix README (lines 58-62; review R3, O06/O07) explicitly leaves transitions into the admin login and systemd, and access to undeclared host domains, to host policy outside the matrix. Within the matrix, the worker has no outgoing transition and no process2 nnp_transition grant (only broker to worker and runtime to container). That, not A24-A32, is what closes it for declared domains after no_new_privs. The claim is stated more broadly than its evidence.
findings.requiredChange: Either narrow the text to 'no transition into any declared domain (the matrix grants planeon_worker_t no transition and no process2 nnp_transition; A29, A30 and A32 for the planeon domains)' and keep 'no execute_no_trans on any type (A60.18)', which already refuses a second exec without a transition. Or add a per-source transition/nnp_transition closure for planeon_worker_t to a future matrix and cite it. Under either option, say that host-policy transitions are bounded by W03's module ('may grant nothing the matrix closes').

findings.finding: The new EDITORIAL kind needs no owner decision and no disposition, and the model puts no limit on where an EDITORIAL item may apply. In scratch I added an EDITORIAL item E3 that replaces 'No CAP_KILL: termination' with 'Holds CAP_KILL: termination' in the BROKER row, with decisions [], and re-pinned the effective file. check() accepted it. So a normative change can enter the effective specification without any owner decision, which the record's own rule ('each item citing its owner decisions') is meant to prevent. RESTATED items are also unconstrained: an item citing an unrelated decided decision (W02d-QB on the gate's SELinux text) passes, and RESTATED items need no disposition.
findings.requiredChange: Restrict EDITORIAL items structurally, for example: allowed only when the current text is the base's first line (title) or its last line (an appended section), and the proposed text keeps that line. Alternatively, list the allowed EDITORIAL ids and their anchors in the model. Optionally require each RESTATED item to name a decision whose text mentions the restated subject, or list the RESTATED ids in notAmended and check that.
Check that decision and item entries are strings before calling set(), or soften the disposition wording. Optionally cross-check obligation references in item text.

findings.location: amendment.json item A7 (BROKER row) and O-T04-AMEND
findings.finding: 'the worker shows Seccomp_filters: 2' holds only if the broker carries exactly one filter. fs/proc/array.c:339-340 prints seccomp.filter_count, kernel/fork.c:1900 copies it to the child, and kernel/seccomp.c:932 increments it in W4. That premise rests on W03 ('install exactly the compiled programs', F10: no systemd seccomp options), and A7 doesn't say so. The A7 source cites kernel/seccomp.c without line numbers.
findings.requiredChange: Add the premise ('the broker runs under exactly its one filter, so ...') or cite the W03 carried requirement, and give the line numbers.

findings.finding: 'W4's setresgid and setresuid leave supplementary groups unchanged, so the broker runs with none (obligation O-W03-GROUPS)' reads as a causal fact, but it is a requirement: the broker must run with none because setresgid/setresuid do not clear them. A10 cites kernel/sys.c:676-838, which is not among the provided v6.12 sources, so I could not check it there. The claim that setresuid/setresgid do not touch group_info is correct.
findings.requiredChange: Change 'so the broker runs with none' to 'so the broker must run with none', and add kernel/sys.c to the pinned sources or drop the line range.

findings.finding: The R1-10 disposition says QW3's reason now reads 'a CAP_SYS_ADMIN holder in the initial namespaces'. That is true in amendment.json and the amendment README. The v2 README still says 'any CAP_SYS_ADMIN holder can lower it in the init namespace (kernel/pid_sysctl.h)', and the v2 allowlists.json decision text still says 'any CAP_SYS_ADMIN holder'.
findings.requiredChange: Align the v2 wording and citation (kernel/pid_sysctl.h:8-32, include/linux/pid_namespace.h:59-67).

questionAnswers.Q1:
Yes. The round-1 verification stands: mm/memfd.c:313-325 and 401-410; kernel/signal.c:814-824 and 846-860 on the pidfd_send_signal path. The init-namespace lowering now has a source: kernel/pid_sysctl.h:8-32 with include/linux/pid_namespace.h:59-67, so for the init namespace pidns_memfd_noexec_scope(NULL) is 0 and the minimum is 0. New kernel claims checked:

- Seccomp_filters is filter_count (array.c:339-340); it is copied on fork (fork.c:1900) and incremented on attach (seccomp.c:932), so the worker shows 2 if the broker has exactly one filter (R2-5).
- kernel/sys.c (A10) is not in the provided sources (R2-6).
